recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Body: Kyle and Serena Denton are community herbalists creating wild-crafted and organic plant medicines out of Milwaukee since 2015. These products work, not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "A Healthy Relationship With Psychedelics", "body": "Mike answers Chance's question about substance use by comparing a good relationship with psychedelics to a good relationship with food or with people: it should leave you nourished, clear, and inspired. He urges weighing risk against reward, checking your intention, treating the substances as tools rather than crutches, and meeting them with respect and reverence, then widens the frame by noting that everyone interacts with drugs daily through tea, coffee, and media. Chance adds that reverence is simply paying attention, and that attention is our spiritual currency."}, {"title": "From Stand-Up Comedy to Mikeadelic", "body": "Mike traces his path from a restless kid who kept asking why and resented being told what to do, to a quest for truth through comedy heroes such as Bill Hicks and George Carlin. He did stand-up in New York, met Dave Smith, co-hosted a libertarian podcast for a few years, then left in 2016 to focus on Mikeadelic, drinking ayahuasca and traveling to Peru along the way. Chance responds that once the gates open, every answer yields more questions, an infinite expansion where everything becomes part of one path."}, {"title": "Cognitive Liberty and Decriminalization", "body": "Chance opens by calling cognitive liberty the foundation of every other liberty and urging listeners to sharpen their rhetoric in 2020. Mike describes joining the Denver mushroom decriminalization push, passing out flyers and speaking out, and calls sovereignty over body, mind, and spirit an innate birthright, citing Graham Hancock's War on Consciousness talk and his own claim that psychedelics quiet the default mode network. Chance adds a riff on cannabis, from sativas and indicas to the upside of legalization."}, {"title": "Compartmentalization, Language, and Scaffolding", "body": "Chance recalls brain scans in which walled-off regions began talking to each other under a psychedelic, then compares that with the corporate compartmentalization he sees in society and calls language the real matrix. Mike stresses that lasting change needs mental scaffolding, with preparation mattering as much as integration, and likens it to researching a trip abroad. Chance links this to the trivium of preparation, experience, and integration, and shares a DMT mandala whose message, in his telling, was to go with the flow."}, {"title": "Shipibo Reciprocity and the Masks of Language", "body": "Mike recounts going to Peru in 2016, where Shipibo healers introduced him to a cosmology of interconnected life and a way of living with balance and reciprocity. Chance contrasts the indigenous sense of being part of nature with the colonial mind, argues that evil merely inverts what is natural, and plays on words: live spelled backward is evil, a persona is a mask, and no noun captures a self that is a process of becoming. His solo closing names letting go as psychedelics' lesson and flow as the goal."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Mike Brancatelli is the host of Mikeadelic, a podcast about the many uses and philosophies connecting psychedelic plant medicine traditions throughout our realm. In this episode, we get trippy and talk about what a healthy relationship with plant medicine looks like, as opposed to the drug-culture created by the toxic modern pharmacopeia. It's a real face-melter, so tuck that ego into bed and kiss it goodnight as we explore the forbidden reaches of our selves.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The One Ring and the Nature of Power", "body": "Asked for his view of the pandemic year, Mike argues that the real division runs between ordinary people and a power elite, and that the true nature of power is best captured by Tolkien's One Ring. He cites a quotation he attributes to Hermann Goering about how fear lets rulers do anything, and says the useful questions are why, and who stands to gain. Chance picks up the Tolkien thread, describing Sauron's hold as fear that collapses once someone stands up to it, and ties the ring to Saturn symbolism."}, {"title": "Smelling Fear and Refusing the Offer", "body": "Chance describes how psychedelic experience taught him to recognize fear as an idea rather than a fact, recalling a brief jolt of alarm at the start of the pandemic that he met by remembering a mushroom journey that turned out to be nothing. From there he argues that society's demands are really offers, a framing he says lets you win the game once you see it. Mike agrees and warns that the real damage comes when people who share this view turn on each other, since public shaming and tribal ostracization make speaking your truth harder."}, {"title": "Dune, Hidden Abilities, and a New Cage", "body": "Mike mentions he has just started reading Dune, and the talk turns to the Butlerian Jihad and the idea that outlawing thinking machines let human psychic abilities flourish, a notion both men grant some truth without endorsing a full anti-tech jihad. The pair float a future show on the book and detour into the gematria of orange and the Orange Catholic Bible. Asked what comes next, Chance reads the Saturn and Jupiter conjunction in Aquarius as a change of outfit for old control rather than a liberation: not a new age but a new cage, though he hopes the shakeup leads some people to refuse cages altogether."}, {"title": "Sovereignty, Natural Law, and Building Outside the System", "body": "Chance answers the question of how to escape technocratic control by rejecting armed revolution, which he says only installs new masters, and pointing instead to building something outside the system that others can choose. He defines sovereignty as non-dependence, starting with growing your own food and securing clean water, and shares Jung's Seven Sermons to the Dead, whose Pleroma and Abraxas frame power as a choice between creating and destroying. Later the talk argues that natural law, meaning conscience, should outrank legal statute, while both men favor local communities of like-hearted people."}, {"title": "Imagination, Vessels, and Word Magic", "body": "Asked how psychedelics shaped his imagination, Mike says they confirmed his sense that reality is layered, eased his fears, and gave him the nerve to try comedy and podcasting, ending on possibility and hope. Chance answers that the inner light needs a container, citing Walter Russell on capturing ideas and calling a podcast or a painting such a vessel, and warns that intelligence without conscience makes a highly effective tool for someone else. The hour closes on word magic, from the older sense of smart as pain to the word onomancy, the magic of names, and a tip to consult old dictionaries."}]

Are you going to get your face blown off?", "author": "Mike Brancatelli", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "Every type of noun that we apply to ourself, or even adjectives for that matter, is never actually true because all that you are is what you are, and that's a process of becoming.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "A lot of people talk about integration, but it's really about the preparation, too, to make sure that you are ready to embark on a journey.", "author": "Mike Brancatelli", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "Returning to the flow state is what everything is all about, in my opinion.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "It's really cool to see that people support someone who's just kind of losing their mind on a microphone, and talking about the things that affect our world and our reality.", "author": "Mike Brancatelli", "portrait": ""}]
